question: Does a fixed-prompt local instruction LLM improve financial-news sentiment over our frozen MiniLM v2 release and the current colleague LinearSVC v2 recipe?
llm_prompt: src/local_llm.py SYSTEM, copied into local artifact before evaluation; no prompt search
training: No new MiniLM training. Reconstruct LinearSVC v2 using pinned reference source, original train plus opinion supplement. Qwen is zero-shot BF16, no fine-tuning or demonstrations.
data: Pinned SEntFiN unanimous-entity native English headlines; 200 per class, seed 20261106. Exclude previous 600 paired ids, normalized duplicates and every available original train/val/test text from both approaches plus the v2 supplement. Translate selected EN to DE with the previous pinned Marian model.
primary_metric: macro_f1_en on 600 fresh human-labelled native English headlines
secondary_metrics: confusion matrices overall and by language
selection: Highest native EN macro-F1; within 0.005 absolute of best prefer lower mean warm batch-one inference latency, then smaller artifact. German MT is a transfer diagnostic, not independent native-DE selection evidence.
latency: Same tower, sequential candidates, 10 warm-up predictions on a non-benchmark text, batch one, tokenizer and CPU/GPU transfers included, CUDA synchronization; excludes model loading, HTML fetch and HTTP. CPU reference in separate pinned environment.
evaluation: Freeze code, prompt, artifact hashes and benchmark before inference. Predict each benchmark text once per candidate. No tuning on this benchmark, no old tests re-evaluated. Save row ids/scores locally and aggregate evidence in Git/MLflow. Bootstrap cached paired predictions only, 1000 replicates seed 20261106.
deployment: Activate only after completed comparison and offline/API tests. Keep previous selected.json untouched; use separate serving_selected.json. Website uses same predictor artifact and /predict contract as evaluation.
limitations: 600 independent headlines plus their translations, not 1200 independent articles
No native German gold or general long-article accuracy claim
Public-corpus LLM pretraining contamination and semantic event overlap unknown
Different training data; comparison is between deployable systems, not isolated architectures
Local hosting removes a cloud inference dependency but does not guarantee availability during GPU, power, disk or process failure
Constrained LLM scores are not calibrated probabilities
